title: Recover rules. Build evidence. Reuse the method.
say: Our approach is a reusable discovery loop. We start with a readable rule, use the mismatches to guide experiments, and turn supported findings into deterministic Python. AI helps investigate; exact comparisons decide what we keep.
support: Opening goes directly to our approach: assume the jury knows the challenge. Assistants used in development include Claude Code and Codex; the submitted calculations are deterministic. This is a human-guided toolkit, not autonomous recovery of arbitrary formulas.
cue: Face camera; then bring up the three-step stack.

title: Turn each mismatch into an experiment.
say: A dictionary-driven loader gives us consistent inputs. We write a baseline, then ask where, when and how it fails. Trees identify conditions; change-point and residual tools suggest conventions. We test alternatives and rerun dependent tasks before integrating a rule.
support: Actual tools: legacy_loader.py, tools/rule_finder.py, tools/change_points.py, tools/residuals.py, tools/convention_search.py. The tree classifies mismatches; it does not establish the true formula. Convention search enumerates supplied candidate sets. Humans select features, propose candidates and assess evidence.
cue: Trace the loop left to right; emphasize testing rather than hypothesis generation alone.

title: Find where the system changed.
say: Applying newer conventions to older policies creates a strong historical pattern. Change-point analysis directs us to the conversion; we then test rounding, age and day-count candidates. The result is a dated rule with evidence. Both curves here show T4 training statements.
support: Source: methodology_sample/era_evidence.csv. Red is the recorded T4 Neuron NG-only experiment from Plots/errors_by_era.csv. Teal is recalculated from the verified latest T4 snapshot and all 34,145 local training rows, with21 mismatches. This is local training evidence, not private accuracy or a fresh NG-only ablation of the final candidate. The annual plot motivates inspecting an era boundary; it does not independently identify the exact day. Current rules use conversion2007-08-11. Residual rates are small but not universally zero.
cue: Point to the older era, then to persistent errors after conversion. Explain carry-forward effects briefly.

title: Use the error shape to propose a formula.
say: Residuals also suggest formulas. This illustrative thirty-one-day charge is about three percent above a fixed monthly charge, suggesting actual-days over three-sixty. Our search tests competing day counts and rounding modes against real diagnostics. A plausible signature still needs exact validation.
support: Illustration: value 10,000, annual rate 1%, elapsed period 31 days. Fixed month: 10,000×0.01/12=8.3333…; Actual/360: 10,000×0.01×31/360=8.6111…. Ratio of unrounded values=31/30=1.03333…. Displayed 8.33 and 8.61 use half-up cents for illustration; the historical era can use truncation. These are not observed policy outputs. Source tools: residuals.implied_ratios, convention_search.search, date_conventions.py.
cue: Point from the 1.033 ratio to the proposed day count; do not describe the toy amounts as measured outcomes.

title: Keep investigating when amounts are missing.
say: For T7, we reused the workflow with weaker evidence. This actual Swiss example crosses the threshold between gross and net proceeds, supporting investigation of penalties. Booking presence constrains applicability; it cannot establish the amount. Public examples add checks, while hidden accuracy remains unresolved.
support: Actual witness BL10002408/event 8, country CH, status E. research/t7_version2_experiments.md records gross tax-currency proceeds 5,042.28 and net 4,941.43; no VST booking. Latest cases.json confirms net CHF base 4,941.43 and no booked tax types. Policy currency is EUR, so label the displayed amounts CHF after conversion, not raw policy amounts. Booking absence supports applicability, not cent-exact tax amounts or remittance. Latest reported evaluated baseline: payout 1/20 and annual 15/20; current TRACE candidate has not been scored in this conversation.

title: New target. Same investigative tools.
say: For another target, we supply new features, candidate formulas and evidence. We reuse the analysis, searches and validation process. Local T0-to-T4 scores exceed ninety-nine point seven percent. Our contribution is a reusable, human-guided method, with clear boundaries around verified results.
support: Local train scores from the full regression: T0 225848/225858, T1 15028/15028, T2 3011/3019, T3 6137/6153, T4 34124/34145. These are not private results. T7 last reported evaluated versions 1/20 payout and 15/20 annual; latest TRACE overlay is unscored. Generality is demonstrated across targets within this challenge, not across arbitrary unseen industries. Decoder formats and relationship browsers require adapters. Maintainability latest local82.5, wall/RSS overhead documented in t7_trace.md.
